title: I trained an AI car to tow a vault and fight police cars (PPO in Unreal Engine 5), and it learned to set traps first
author: Dry_Lie_5593
selftext:
**Hi everyone,**

I wanted to share a small reinforcement learning project I've been working on in Unreal Engine 5, inspired by the vault chase scene in Fast & Furious 5. I'd really appreciate any feedback.

**\*\*Setup\*\***

\- Two cars on a looping track with many sharp turns, defined by a spline

\- A police car trained with PPO to patrol along the road (then frozen as a fixed opponent). It was never taught to dodge, so it simply plows into whatever is in its way

\- A race car towing a one-ton vault, trained with PPO to flip police cars

\- Both agents use the same action space: throttle, brake, steering

\- Training: neural network on GPU, physics simulation on CPU (the CPU is the bottleneck)

**\*\*Reward function for the race car\*\***

\- Large reward: flipping a police car, or steering the vault into one

\- Small reward: staying on the road and driving in the right direction

\- Small penalty: getting hit by the police car, or driving the wrong way

\- Large penalty: leaving the track, or being stuck for more than 3 seconds

**\*\*What happened\*\***

1. \*\*Bullied.\*\* Early on, the car just lay still and took the hits. Being hit was cheap, while moving the vault usually threw the car off the track, which was expensive. This looks like a classic local optimum.

2. \*\*Trap.\*\* After a while, it started dragging the vault onto the police patrol route, waiting, and swerving away at the last moment so the police car hit the vault. This technically satisfies "vault hits police car", so it's a nice example of reward hacking / specification gaming. It wasn't what I had in mind.

3. \*\*Hero.\*\* I increased the penalty for standing still, moving slowly, or getting stuck (reward shaping). The trap disappeared, and the car started charging at the police car, timing its speed and angle to launch it, and sometimes dodging at the last second so the police car hits the vault behind it.

I turned this into a video that explains the basics (observation/action/reward, PPO, local optima, reward hacking) in a light-hearted way, mainly for people who are new to RL:

[**https://youtu.be/UUoUOKSQ8FQ**](https://youtu.be/UUoUOKSQ8FQ)

I'd love to hear your thoughts, especially:

\- Is there a better way to discourage the "wait and trap" strategy than penalizing idle time?

\- Any suggestions for making training with a towed object more stable?



***Thanks for reading, and I'm happy to answer questions about the setup.***

comments.author: thundergenie
comments.body: Parking the vault on the patrol route and letting the police drive into it is a very Fast & Furious way to read a reward function.
